p.src: Now, Lai Da led Jia Qin out, and after an uneventful night they quietly awaited Jia Zheng's return. The young Buddhist and Taoist nuns, meanwhile, were overjoyed to be back in the garden and wanted to stroll about everywhere before preparing to enter the palace the next day. Unexpectedly, Lai Da ordered the old women and pages who guarded the garden to watch them; they were given food and drink, but forbidden to move so much as a step away. The girls could make neither head nor tail of it and had no choice but to sit there until dawn. Although the maids throughout the garden knew that the young nuns had been brought in for possible service in the palace, they did not know the full reason behind it.

p.src: Early the next morning, just as Jia Zheng was about to leave his office, registers of estimates and expenditures for municipal works in two provinces were sent down from the tribunal for immediate examination. Unable to return home, he sent word to Jia Lian: “When Lai Da returns, you must question him thoroughly. Deal with the matter as it ought to be dealt with; there is no need to wait for me.” On receiving the order, Jia Lian was at first pleased for Qin's sake, but then reflected, “If I dispose of the matter without leaving the slightest trace of anything amiss, Jia Zheng may grow suspicious. I had better report to Second Madam and ask her advice. Then, even if the decision displeases the master, I shall not bear too much responsibility.” Having made up his mind, he went inside to see Lady Wang and explained, “Yesterday the master became angry when he saw the placard and had Qin and the Buddhist and Taoist nuns brought into the residence for investigation. Today he has no time to inquire into such a scandalous affair, so he told me to report to you, Madam, and deal with it as you see fit. I have therefore come to ask how you wish the matter handled.” Lady Wang was astonished. “What is the meaning of this?” she exclaimed. “If Qin has truly behaved in such a way, how can he still be considered a member of our family? Yet whoever posted that placard is detestable too. Are such allegations things one may recklessly bandy about? Did you actually ask Qin whether there was any truth in it?” “I questioned him just now,” replied Jia Lian. “But consider, Madam: whether or not he did it, would anyone admit to having committed such a disgraceful act even if he had? Still, I do not think Qin would dare do such a thing. He knew that Her Highness might summon those girls at any time; what would become of him if a scandal arose? In my opinion, it would not be hard to get at the truth; but if we do, how would you have us deal with it?” “Where are those girls now?” asked Lady Wang. “They are all confined in the garden,” replied Jia Lian. “Do the young ladies know about it?” asked Lady Wang. “They probably all understand that the girls are being prepared for service in the palace. Nothing else has been mentioned outside,” said Jia Lian. “That is well,” said Lady Wang. “These creatures must not be kept here a moment longer. I wanted to send them away before, but you all said it would be better to keep them. And now has it not led to trouble? Have Lai Da and his men take them away. Find out carefully whether they have relatives at home, locate their documents, spend a few dozen taels to hire a boat, and appoint a trustworthy man to escort them back to their native places. Return them together with all their papers, and then we shall be rid of the affair. If one or two have behaved badly, it would be far too cruel to force every one of them to return to secular life. If we hand them over to the official matchmakers here, even though we ask no price for them, those women will sell them for profit without the slightest regard for whether they live or die.

p.src: As for Qin, give him a severe scolding. Except for sacrifices and family celebrations, tell him not to come here without good reason. He had better take care not to encounter the master in a fit of anger, or he will suffer more than he can bear. And tell the accounts office to strike this item of allowance from its books. Also send someone to Water Moon Convent with the master's command: except when they go there to tend the family graves and burn offerings, no gentlemen of our clan are to be received there. If the slightest unsavory rumor arises again, the old abbess herself will be driven out along with the rest.”

p.src: Jia Lian agreed to everything. Going out, he relayed Lady Wang's instructions to Lai Da: “This is Madam's decision. Carry it out exactly as she says. When it is done, tell me, and I shall report back to Madam. Make haste and see to it. When the master returns, report to him in accordance with Madam's instructions.” On hearing this, Lai Da said, “Our Madam truly has the heart of a Buddha. These creatures are to be escorted home. Since Madam is so compassionate, we must choose a good man for the task. Brother Qin may as well be left to you, Second Master, to discipline. As for the person who posted that placard, I shall find a way to uncover him, and then he must be punished severely.” Jia Lian nodded. “Very well,” he said. He dealt with Jia Qin at once. Lai Da promptly led the young nuns and the others out and went to carry out the plan. When Jia Zheng returned home that evening, Jia Lian and Lai Da reported the whole matter to him. Jia Zheng was by nature a man who disliked needless trouble, so after hearing their report he let the matter drop. The local scoundrels alone, hearing that the Jia household had released twenty-four young women, all began to entertain designs upon them. Whether those girls ultimately succeeded in returning home cannot be known, and it would be difficult to speculate upon their fate.

p.src: Now that Daiyu was gradually recovering and all was quiet in the garden, Zijuan heard that the nuns were preparing to serve at the Palace. Not knowing what the occasion might be, she went to Grandmother Jia's quarters to inquire. There she happened upon Yuanyang coming downstairs, and as they had nothing to do, they sat chatting and brought up the matter of the nuns. Yuanyang said in surprise, “I haven't heard anything about it. When she returns, we can ask Mistress Lian and find out.” As they spoke, two women from Fu Shi's household arrived to pay their respects to Grandmother Jia, and Yuanyang was about to accompany them upstairs. But as Grandmother Jia was taking her midday nap, the two women merely left a message with Yuanyang and went home. Zijuan asked, “Which household sent them?” Yuanyang replied, “What tiresome people! Just because they have a daughter who is rather pretty, they parade her like some priceless treasure. They are always telling the Old Lady how beautiful and kindhearted their young lady is, how accomplished in manners, how spare and refined in speech, how deft at needlework, and how well she can read, write, and reckon. They say she is perfectly filial toward her elders and unfailingly gentle even with the servants. Every time they come, they reel off this whole long rigmarole for the Old Lady. I'm thoroughly sick of hearing it. Those old women are truly insufferable. Yet our Old Lady happens to love such talk. The Old Lady is one thing, but there is also Baoyu. Ordinarily the very sight of an old woman annoys him, yet for some reason he never minds the old women from their household. Isn't that strange! Only the other day they came saying that ever so many families had proposed marriage to their young lady, but their master had refused every one of them, for in his heart he would consent only to an alliance with a family like ours. First praising their girl and then flattering us, they have quite stirred the Old Lady's interest.” Zijuan was stunned to hear this, but feigned indifference and asked, “If the Old Lady likes her, why doesn't she simply betroth her to Baoyu?” Yuanyang was just about to explain why when a voice from upstairs announced, “The Old Lady is awake.” Yuanyang hurried upstairs.

p.src: Zijuan had no choice but to rise and leave, returning to the garden. As she walked, she thought, “Can there be only one Baoyu under heaven, that you must long for him and I must long for him too? Our young lady has grown more infatuated than ever. From the way she behaves, it is certain her whole heart is set on Baoyu. If her repeated illnesses aren't because of this, what else could cause them! This household is already in turmoil over the golden one and the silvery one; if some Miss Fu is added as well, there will be no end of trouble. I believe Baoyu's heart is with our young lady too, but from what Yuanyang said, one would think he falls in love with every girl he sees. Wouldn't that mean our young lady has been tormenting herself for nothing?” Zijuan had begun by worrying about Daiyu, but the further her thoughts ran, the less she knew what to make of it all, and tears came to her eyes. She wanted to tell Daiyu not to worry needlessly, yet feared that doing so would only distress her; but to stand by and see her like this was pitiful too. She turned the matter over and over until irritation suddenly seized her, and she spat at herself, saying, “Why are you fretting over someone else's affairs? Even if Miss Lin truly marries Baoyu, her temperament will make her difficult to serve. Baoyu may be sweet-natured, but he is always biting off more than he can chew. Here I am urging others not to worry foolishly, when I am the one worrying foolishly myself. From now on, I shall devote myself to serving my young lady and meddle in nothing else!” Once she had resolved upon this, her mind actually felt at peace. When she returned to the Xiaoxiang Lodge, she found Daiyu sitting alone on the kang, sorting through drafts of poems, essays, and lyrics she had written in the past. Looking up and seeing Zijuan enter, she asked, “Where have you been?” Zijuan replied, “I went to see the other girls today.” Daiyu said, “I suppose you went to see Sister Xiren?” Zijuan replied, “What would I seek her out for?” Only then did Daiyu realize that the question had slipped from her lips, and she felt embarrassed. She spat and said, “What business is it of mine whom you went to see! Go and bring me some tea.”

p.src: Zijuan laughed inwardly too, then went out to pour the tea. Just then she heard a great clamor of voices rising from the garden. Not knowing what had happened, she poured the tea while sending someone to inquire. The messenger returned and said, “Several of the crabapple trees at Happy Red Court had withered, and no one had even bothered to water them. Yesterday Baoyu went over and noticed what looked like buds on the branches. No one believed him, so they paid no attention. Then suddenly today the crabapple burst into splendid bloom. Everyone was amazed and is scrambling to see it. Even the Old Lady and the ladies have been stirred into coming to see the flowers. That is why Mistress Li has ordered the dead leaves and withered branches cleared from the garden, and those people are calling everyone to the task.” Daiyu had heard the commotion too. Learning that the Old Lady was coming, she changed her clothes and sent Xueyan to find out what was happening. “If the Old Lady has arrived, come and tell me at once.” Before long Xueyan came running back. “The Old Lady, the ladies, and ever so many others are here. Please come at once, miss.” Daiyu glanced at herself in the mirror, smoothed her hair at the temples, and went to Happy Red Court leaning on Zijuan’s arm. She found the Old Lady already seated on the couch where Baoyu usually reclined and greeted her: “I hope you are well, Grandmother.” Stepping back, she greeted Ladies Xing and Wang, then exchanged courtesies with Li Wan, Tanchun, Xichun, and Xing Xiuyan. Only Xifeng had not come because she was ill. Shi Xiangyun’s uncle had been transferred back to the capital and had taken her home; Xue Baoqin had gone to stay with her elder sister’s family; and because of the many disturbances in the garden, Aunt Li had taken the Li sisters to live outside. Thus Daiyu saw only a few people there that day. After chatting and laughing awhile, they discussed how strangely the flowers had bloomed. Grandmother Jia said, “These flowers ought to bloom in the third month. It may be the eleventh month now, but since the seasons are late this year, it may still be reckoned the tenth. This is the weather of the little spring, so the flowers may well have opened because it has been warm.” Lady Wang said, “You have seen a great deal, Old Lady, and what you say is quite right. There is nothing strange about it.” Lady Xing said, “I heard this tree has been withered for a whole year. There must be some reason why it has bloomed out of season now.” Li Wan smiled. “What the Old Lady and the ladies say is all quite true. But in my foolish way of thinking, some happy event must be coming to Baoyu, and this flower has blossomed first to announce it.” Tanchun said nothing, but thought, “This flower can hardly be a good omen. As a rule, what follows the natural order prospers, while what defies it perishes. Plants sense the course of fortune; when they bloom out of season, there must be some evil portent.” She merely felt it would be improper to say so aloud. Daiyu alone was moved by the suggestion of a happy event and said cheerfully, “Long ago, the Tian family had a redbud tree. When the three brothers divided their household, the tree withered.

p.src: Later it moved the brothers to live together again, and the redbud flourished once more. This shows that plants too respond to human beings. Now that Second Cousin is applying himself earnestly to his studies and Uncle is pleased with him, that tree has blossomed too.” Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang were delighted to hear this. “Miss Lin’s comparison is sensible and most meaningful,” they said. While they were speaking, Jia She, Jia Zheng, Jia Huan, and Jia Lan all came in to see the flowers. Jia She said, “In my opinion, we should cut it down. This must be the work of some flower demon.” Jia Zheng said, “Regard nothing as strange, and the strangeness will defeat itself. There is no need to cut it down. Just leave it alone.” Grandmother Jia overheard him and exclaimed, “Who is talking such nonsense here? When a happy and fortunate event is coming to the family, why speak of strange things? If it brings good fortune, you may all enjoy it; if it brings ill fortune, I alone shall bear it. You are not to talk such nonsense.” At this Jia Zheng dared say no more and withdrew awkwardly with Jia She and the others.

She ordered, “Baoyu, Huan, and Lan must each compose a poem to celebrate the occasion. Miss Lin has only just recovered from her illness, so do not tax her. p.src: When Grandmother Jia had heard them all, she said, “I know little about poetry, but to my ear Lan’s is the best. Huan’s is not good. Come up, all of you, and eat.” Seeing how pleased Grandmother Jia was, Baoyu grew more animated than ever. Then he remembered: “The crabapple died in the same year that Qingwen died. Now that it has flourished again, surely everyone in our court will fare well. But Qingwen can never come back to life as the flower has done.” In an instant, his joy turned to sorrow. Then he suddenly recalled that a few days earlier Qiaojie had said Xifeng intended to bring Wu’er in to fill the vacancy. Perhaps the flower had bloomed for her—who could say? His sorrow turned back to joy, and he resumed his laughing conversation.

p.src: Grandmother Jia remained seated for quite some time before returning, supported by Zhenzhu. Lady Wang and the others followed after her. Just then Ping'er came forward smiling and said, “Our mistress heard that the Old Lady was here admiring the blossoms. Since she could not come herself, she sent me to attend upon the Old Lady and the ladies. She has also sent two lengths of red silk for Master Bao to wrap around the tree as a congratulatory gift.” Xiren came forward to receive the silk and presented it to Grandmother Jia for inspection. Grandmother Jia laughed. “That girl Feng always knows how to do something that is at once proper, novel, and delightful.” Smiling, Xiren said to Ping'er, “When you go back, thank Second Mistress on Master Bao's behalf. If this is a happy omen, may we all share in its joy.” Hearing this, Grandmother Jia laughed. “Oh dear, I had quite forgotten! Though that girl Feng is ill, she is still the one who thinks of everything, and her gift is most apt.” As she spoke, everyone accompanied her away. In private, Ping'er told Xiren, “Mistress says that since these blossoms have opened so strangely, you should cut a strip of red silk and hang it on the tree, so the omen may be turned toward a happy event. From now on, you need not keep speaking of it indiscriminately as something uncanny.” Xiren nodded her assent and saw Ping'er out. But no more of this.

p.src: Now Baoyu had originally been resting at home that day in a round-cut fur coat. After seeing the tree in bloom, however, he kept coming out to look at it, admire it, sigh over it, and cherish it, investing that single tree with all the countless joys and sorrows, meetings and partings, in his heart. Suddenly hearing that Grandmother Jia was coming, he changed into a close-sleeved jacket trimmed with fox underarm fur, put on an outer coat lined with black fox-leg fur, and went out to welcome her. In his haste to change, he had neglected to hang the Magic Jade around his neck. Later, after Grandmother Jia had left, he changed back into his former clothes. When Xiren saw that nothing hung from Baoyu's neck, she asked, “Where is the jade?” Baoyu replied, “I took it off when I was changing in that rush just now and put it on the kang table. I did not wear it.” Xiren looked back, but there was no jade on the table. She searched everywhere, yet found no trace of it, and broke out in a cold sweat from fright. Baoyu said, “There is no need to panic. It must be somewhere in the room. Ask the others and you will find out.” Supposing that Sheyue and the others had hidden it to frighten him as a prank, Xiren said to them with a smile, “You little wretches, even a prank must have its limits. Where have you hidden it? Do not tell me you have truly lost it, or none of us will survive the consequences.” Sheyue and the others all grew solemn. “What are you talking about? A prank is a prank and a joke is a joke, but this is no trifling matter. Do not talk such nonsense. You must have lost your wits. Think carefully—think where you put it. And now you are casting the blame on us without cause.” Seeing their manner and realizing they were not joking, Xiren cried anxiously, “Merciful Heaven and Bodhisattva! My precious young master, where in the world did you put it?” Baoyu said, “I remember quite clearly putting it on the kang table. You must keep looking.” Xiren, Sheyue, Qiuwen, and the others dared not let anyone know, so they all searched secretly in every corner. After searching in turmoil for most of the day without the slightest result, even emptying chests and overturning trunks, they could think of nowhere else to look. They began to suspect that one of the people who had entered earlier might have picked it up and taken it away. Xiren said, “Everyone who came in knows that this jade is as precious as life itself. Who would dare take it? Whatever you do, do not raise the alarm yet. Hurry and make inquiries everywhere. If one of the young ladies found it and hid it to frighten us, kneel and beg her to return it. If a little maid stole it, we need not report her to our superiors once we discover who she is; we may give her anything she wants in exchange for it. This is no small matter. If it is truly lost, the consequences will be even graver than if Master Bao himself were lost.” Just as Sheyue and Qiuwen were about to leave, Xiren hurried after them and cautioned, “Do not question those who ate here earlier just yet. If we fail to find it and stir up further trouble instead, matters will be even worse.”

p.src: Following her instructions, Sheyue and the others split up to make inquiries everywhere, but no one knew anything, and everyone was startled and suspicious. When Sheyue and the others returned, they all stood dumbfounded, staring at one another. Baoyu too was stunned with fright. In her desperation, Xiren could do nothing but weep helplessly. There was nowhere left to search, yet they dared not report the loss. Everyone in Happy Red Court was so terrified that they stood as still as figures carved from wood or molded from clay.

p.src: While everyone stood there dumbfounded, all those who had heard the news arrived from every quarter. Tanchun ordered the garden gates shut. She first sent an old maidservant with two maids to search everywhere again, while having it announced that whoever found the jade would receive a handsome reward in silver. Everyone wanted first to clear themselves of suspicion and, second, had heard of the generous reward, so they searched frantically without regard for life or limb, even looking inside the privies. Yet the jade seemed as elusive as an embroidery needle: though they searched all day, not a trace of it appeared. Li Wan grew desperate and said, “This is no laughing matter. I must say something rather discourteous.” “What is it?” everyone asked. Li Wan said, “Now that matters have come to this, we cannot stand on ceremony. Apart from Baoyu, everyone now in the garden is a woman. I must ask all you ladies and young mistresses to have the maids who came with you undress so that we may search them. If it is not among them, we shall have the maids search the old women and the servants assigned to rough work.” Everyone said, “That makes sense too. With so many people bustling about, all sorts have become mixed together. Doing this will also clear your names.” Tanchun alone said nothing. The maids were also willing to clear themselves of suspicion. Pinger stepped forward first and said, “Begin by searching me.” They each loosened their own clothes, and Li Wan searched them all in rapid succession. Tanchun reproached Li Wan: “Sister-in-law, have you too begun behaving like those good-for-nothings? If someone stole it, would they still keep it on their person? Besides, the thing is a treasure in this household, but outside it would be worthless to anyone unaware of what it is. Why steal it? I think someone must be playing a malicious prank.” Hearing this, and noticing that Huan was not there, everyone remembered how he had run all over the rooms the previous day. They all suspected him but were unwilling to say so aloud. Tanchun continued, “The only one who would play such a prank is Huan. Send someone to summon him here quietly. Coax him in private and have him hand it over; then frighten him into keeping silent about it. That will settle the matter.” Everyone nodded in agreement.

p.src: Li Wan then said to Pinger, “Only you can go and get to the bottom of this.” Pinger agreed and hurried away. Before long, she returned with Huan. Everyone pretended that nothing was amiss. They had a bowl of tea brewed and set in the inner room, then deliberately made excuses to withdraw. Since Pinger had been told to coax him, she smiled and asked, “Your second brother’s jade is missing. Have you seen it?” Jia Huan’s face immediately flushed dark purple. Glaring at her, he said, “Someone else loses something, and once again you summon me for questioning and suspect me. Am I some thief with a criminal record?” Seeing his reaction, Pinger dared not press him further. She smiled conciliatorily and said, “That is not what I meant. We only wondered whether Third Master might have taken it to frighten them, so I merely asked if you had seen it, to help them with their search.” Jia Huan said, “His jade was on his own person. Whether anyone saw it should be asked of him—why ask me? There are plenty of people forever fawning over him! Whenever he gets something good, no one comes to ask me; but the moment he loses something, they come questioning me!” With that, he rose and walked out. No one felt able to stop him. Baoyu, meanwhile, became anxious and said, “It is this wretched thing that has caused all the trouble. I do not want it anymore. You need not make any more commotion either. Once Huan leaves, he is certain to shout about it until the whole compound knows. Will that not cause an even greater uproar?” Xiren and the others were so distraught that they began weeping again. “Dear little master, you may think losing the jade is of no consequence, but if the elders learn of it, every one of us will be torn to pieces!” As they spoke, they burst into loud sobs.

p.src: Everyone grew still more distressed. Knowing that the matter could not be concealed, they had no choice but to agree upon an account they could later give Grandmother Jia and the others. Baoyu said, “There is no need for you to discuss it. Just insist that I smashed it, and that will be the end of it.” Pinger said, “Oh, my dear master, how easily you say that! If the elders ask why you smashed it, that would still mean death for them. And suppose they demand the shattered pieces—what shall we do then?” Baoyu said, “Then say instead that I lost it when I went out the other day.” Everyone considered this. It might just pass muster, except that for the past two days he had neither gone to school nor visited anywhere else. Baoyu said, “Why not? Three days ago I went to Prince Nan’an’s residence to watch a play. Say I lost it that day.” Tanchun said, “That will not do either. If it was lost the other day, why was it not reported that same day?” As everyone racked their brains trying to embellish a lie, they heard Lady Zhao approaching, weeping and shouting: “You lose something and do not search for it yourselves, yet you have Huan secretly interrogated and tortured! I have brought Huan here. I may as well hand him over to you people who only know how to kick a man when he is down. Kill him or cut him to pieces, as you please!” With that, she shoved Huan forward and said, “You are a thief—confess at once!” Huan was so enraged that he too began crying and shouting.

p.src: Li Wan was just about to calm them when a maid came in and announced, “Madam is here.” Xiren and the others now wished the ground would swallow them, while Baoyu and the rest hurried out to receive her. For the moment, Concubine Zhao did not dare utter another word and followed them out. Seeing alarm on every face, Lady Wang now believed what she had just heard and asked, “Has that jade truly been lost?” No one dared answer. Lady Wang entered the room, sat down, and summoned Xiren. Terrified, Xiren hastily knelt and, with tears in her eyes, was about to explain. “Get up,” said Lady Wang. “Quickly send people to search carefully. Panicking will only make matters worse.” Xiren was too choked with sobs to speak. Fearing that Xiren would tell the truth, Baoyu said, “Madam, this has nothing to do with Xiren. The other day, when I went to Prince Nan’an’s residence to see a play, I lost it on the way.” “Why did you not look for it that very day?” asked Lady Wang. “I was afraid they would find out,” Baoyu replied, “so I did not tell them. I had Beiming and the others search everywhere outside.” “Nonsense!” said Lady Wang. Do not Xiren and the others attend you whenever you change your clothes? Whenever a young master returns from an outing, they demand an explanation if so much as a handkerchief or purse is missing. How could they fail to ask about the loss of this jade?” Baoyu had no answer. Hearing this, Concubine Zhao grew triumphant and hastily interjected, “So even when something is lost outside, Huan is blamed for it!” Before she could finish, Lady Wang snapped, “We are discussing this matter here, and still you come out with such pointless remarks!” Concubine Zhao dared say no more. Li Wan and Tanchun then gave Lady Wang a truthful account of everything. Lady Wang too became so distressed that her tears fell like rain, and she resolved to report the matter to Grandmother Jia and question the people who had come over from Lady Xing’s quarters.

p.src: Though ill, Xifeng also heard that Baoyu had lost his jade. Learning that Lady Wang had come over and knowing she could not avoid the matter, she made her way into the Garden leaning on Feng’er. Just as Lady Wang rose to leave, Xifeng said in a frail, delicate voice, “My respects, Madam.” Baoyu and the others came over and asked after Xifeng’s health. Lady Wang said to her, “Have you heard too? Is this not extraordinary? It vanished the moment no one was looking, and now it cannot be found. Think carefully: from the maids in the Old Lady’s quarters down to your own Ping’er, whose hands might be untrustworthy, and who might be spiteful enough to do this? I mean to report it to the Old Lady and have the matter thoroughly investigated. Otherwise Baoyu’s very lifeline will have been severed.” Xifeng replied, “There are so many people in our household, coming and going with all sorts of business. As the old saying goes, ‘You may know a man’s face, but not his heart.’ Who can guarantee that any one of them is honest? But now that such a commotion has been raised, everyone already knows. If the thief realizes that Madam means to uncover the culprit and that discovery will leave no place even to bury the body, desperation may drive that person to destroy the jade and wipe out the evidence. What could we do then? In my foolish opinion, we should merely say that Baoyu never cared for it and tossed it away, so its loss is of no great consequence. We need only keep the matter strictly contained and prevent the Old Lady and Master from learning of it. Once that story has been put about, we can secretly send people to investigate everywhere and trick the culprit into bringing it out. Then we shall recover the jade and have firm grounds for fixing the guilt. What does Madam think?” Lady Wang hesitated for quite some time before saying, “What you say is reasonable enough, but how can we possibly conceal it from the Master?” She then called Huan over and said, “Your second brother’s jade has been lost. You were merely asked one question, so why did you start shouting the matter everywhere? If your shouting lets the secret out and the culprit destroys it, we shall see whether you are allowed to go on living!” Jia Huan burst into frightened tears. “I will never shout about it again,” he said. After hearing this, Concubine Zhao dared not say another word. Lady Wang then instructed everyone, “There must still be somewhere you have failed to search. It was safe and sound here in the house; surely it cannot have flown away. But no one is to spread the news. I give Xiren three days to find it. If it is still missing after three days, I fear we shall no longer be able to hide the truth, and none of you need expect another peaceful day.” With that, she told Xifeng to accompany her to Lady Xing’s quarters to discuss how they might trace the culprit. But no more of this for now.

Lady Wang hesitated for quite some time before saying, “What you say is reasonable enough, but how can we possibly conceal it from the Master?”
She then called Huan over and said, “Your second brother’s jade has been lost. You were merely asked one question, so why did you start shouting the matter everywhere?
If your shouting lets the secret out and the culprit destroys it, we shall see whether you are allowed to go on living!”
Jia Huan burst into frightened tears. “I will never shout about it again,” he said.
After hearing this, Concubine Zhao dared not say another word.
Lady Wang then instructed everyone, “There must still be somewhere you have failed to search. It was safe and sound here in the house; surely it cannot have flown away.
But no one is to spread the news.
I give Xiren three days to find it. If it is still missing after three days, I fear we shall no longer be able to hide the truth, and none of you need expect another peaceful day.”
With that, she told Xifeng to accompany her to Lady Xing’s quarters to discuss how they might trace the culprit.
But no more of this for now.

p.src: Everyone felt a little calmer and waited blankly for Xiuyan to return. As they waited in a daze, they saw Baoyu's page Beiming beckoning from outside the door and calling for a young maid to come out quickly. The young maid hurried outside. Beiming said, “Hurry inside and tell our Second Master, and all the madams, mistresses, and young ladies within, that I have tremendous good news!” “Just tell me quickly,” said the maid. “Why make such a tiresome fuss?” Clapping his hands and laughing, Beiming said, “Let me tell you, miss: once you go in and report it, both of us will receive a reward. What do you suppose it is? I have come with reliable news about Second Master Bao's jade!” What happened next will be revealed in the following chapter.
